title: Real AI Agent Attacks and What Would Have Stopped Them — Andrey Rybka, Bloomberg
talk_summary: A security talk cataloguing real agent incidents (prompt injection, DNS exfiltration, cross-tenant data leaks, supply-chain MCP backdoors, prod DB wipes) and the layered controls that would have stopped each.

takeaways.technique: Rule of two for agent actions
takeaways.what_they_do: Classify each action by three properties—untrusted input, sensitive data, external action—and require human sign-off whenever all three coincide.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can have untrusted input, sensitive data, external action, and you can pick any one of the two of the three actually, and then if you need all three, you need human sign off

takeaways.technique: Deterministic invocation broker + budgets that halt
takeaways.what_they_do: Route every tool call through a deterministic broker outside the model with hard rate limits and budgets that stop execution, not just alert.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Make sure there are budgets that halt, not just alert.

takeaways.technique: One agent, one scoped identity; no low-priv→high-priv agent calls
takeaways.what_they_do: Give each agent its own short-lived, audience-bound credentials and block low-privilege agents from invoking higher-privilege ones.
takeaways.evidence_quote: a low privileged agent was instructed to recruit a more powerful one, which copied the data and raised privileges

takeaways.technique: Delay ingest for third-party packages/MCP servers
takeaways.what_they_do: Don't adopt a package or MCP server on release day; wait a week or two so malicious versions get caught, plus supply-chain verification.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Don't ingest every package on day zero. Ingest it maybe in a week or two.

takeaways.what_they_do: Sandbox runtimes with all outbound traffic denied by default, explicitly covering DNS lookups, since data can be smuggled via DNS.
takeaways.evidence_quote: We want default deny for all outbound traffic, that includes DNS.

takeaways.technique: Deterministic controls outside the model; prompts don't enforce
takeaways.what_they_do: Treat model instructions as advisory and put enforcement in deterministic code that checks and logs every call, with a kill switch.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Governance prompts us deterministic code enforces.
